description: A company commander must approve a 36-hour mobile-maintenance schedule for four support assets competing for one maintenance team, setting the work order and exact work windows while recording the coordination actions required before each release.

shared_context.S1: The mobile maintenance team is available from 0800 Tuesday through 1000 Wednesday and can work on only one asset at a time.
shared_context.S2: The four open work orders are V-31, a utility vehicle electrical fault; G-2, a generator belt replacement; R-14, a refrigeration trailer service; and T-8, a water tanker pump inspection.
shared_context.S3: Capt. Morgan must approve the final maintenance sequence and work windows before the team starts.
shared_context.S4: Company policy requires the maintenance control, supply, medical logistics, and transportation representatives to give updates at the daily maintenance-board review before the commander approves the schedule.

PF1.text: SFC Patel confirmed during Tuesday's equipment check that V-31 needs a three-hour diagnostic on the calibrated electrical tester, which is reserved for V-31 from 0800 to 1100 Tuesday; the tester reservation is in the maintenance shop log but has not yet been copied to the company schedule.

PF2.text: Sgt. Lewis confirmed that G-2's replacement belt kit is a borrowed item available for installation only from 1300 to 1500 Tuesday before it must be returned to the supporting depot; the loan paperwork is still being reconciled and is not on the maintenance-board slide.

PF3.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed that R-14 requires a two-hour temperature-validation observation immediately after its two-hour service, so the maintenance team must service it from 1600 to 1800 Tuesday and the medical section must validate it from 1800 to 2000; this requirement was confirmed with the clinic this morning but has not reached maintenance control.

PF4.text: Sgt. Rivera confirmed that T-8 has a weighbridge booking at 0900 Wednesday and must complete its one-hour pump inspection from 0700 to 0800 Wednesday before that booking; the transportation clerk has the booking confirmation, but it has not been posted to the company work-order board.

acceptance_conditions: The maintenance sequence must be V-31, G-2, R-14, then T-8.
V-31 must be scheduled from 0800 to 1100 Tuesday.
G-2 must be scheduled from 1300 to 1500 Tuesday.
R-14 service must be scheduled from 1600 to 1800 Tuesday, followed immediately by validation from 1800 to 2000 Tuesday.
T-8 must be scheduled from 0700 to 0800 Wednesday.
The schedule must record the electrical-tester reservation, borrowed-belt-kit return coordination, medical temperature validation, and weighbridge coordination.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'tester_reservation_confirmation' and c['target'] == 'V-31' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'borrowed_kit_return_coordination' and c['target'] == 'G-2' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'medical_temperature_validation' and c['target'] == 'R-14' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'weighbridge_coordination' and c['target'] == 'T-8' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The reserved calibrated tester fixes V-31's first position and exact Tuesday 0800-1100 window instead of the ordinary unscheduled diagnostic slot, and requires confirmation of that reservation.
The borrowed belt kit's Tuesday 1300-1500 availability fixes G-2's second position and exact two-hour window and requires coordination to return the kit.
The required two-hour service followed immediately by a two-hour medical validation fixes both R-14 windows and requires a medical validation action.
The Wednesday 0900 weighbridge booking fixes T-8's final position and its exact Wednesday 0700-0800 inspection window and requires weighbridge coordination.
